answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying one verified identity to one slashable bond in the mesa vault, then pricing influence quadratically: casting n votes costs n squared jade credits. Splitting into k identities would cut the raw quadratic fee, but each fake must pass its own personhood check and lock its own bond, so an attacker pays k full bonds plus k checks while an honest agent pays one. A caught double-vote slashes the whole bond. That makes a gale of throwaway identities cost far more than honest play, and keeps each jade stake answerable to a single identity.
